sentences.text:
Writ Petition No.30564 of 2015
O R D E R:

This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
"......to issue an appropriate Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus to declare the action of the respondent authorities in proposing to disburse /release the compensation amount to some unconcerned/third parties in respect of the petitioners land admeasuring 2415.16 Sq. Yards in Sy.Nos.453 and 501/A/B/E situated at Alugunuru Village, Thimmapur Mandal,
Karimnagar District, in spite of the objections submitted on 30.3.2015 and 20.8.2015 as being illegal, arbitrary and unjust and consequently direct the respondent authorities to pay the compensation after verifying the revenue records and to grant such other relief or reliefs......"

2. It is the case of the petitioner that his grandfather was the absolute owner and possessor of the lands in Sy.Nos.453 and 501 to an extent of Ac.1-14 gts and Ac.7-02 gts, Sy.No.49/b/5/1/2 to an extent of Ac.0-12 gts., Sy.No.49/b/6/1/2 to an extent of Ac.0-12 gts., and Sy.No.49/b/2/1/2 to an extent of Ac.0-12 gts., of Alugunuru Village, Thimmapur Mandal, Karimnagar District and after the death of his grandfather, his father and his three brothers have succeeded the said lands.

While so,
the State Government has proposed to acquire the said lands for the purpose of widening and extending the existing road to 4 way lane of Hyderabad-Karimnagar-Ramagundam respectively and respondent No.2 issued notification, dated 18.10.2013 for acquiring lands to an extent of 2415.16 square yards in Sy.Nos.453 and 501/A/B/E and passed an award for payment of compensation amount.

The grievance of the petitioner is that respondent No.4 in collusion with the Village Revenue Officer and without verifying the records pertaining to the said lands, have included the names of some unconcerned/third parties in respect of the above mentioned lands and are making attempts to release/disburse the compensation to the said persons.

3. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4 placed written instructions vide Lr.No.B/1530/2012, dated 04.01.2016 before this Court, wherein it is stated that the compensation of Rs.2,49,63,283/- was awarded to the lands forming part of Sy.Nos.453 and 501 admeasuring 2415.16 sq. yards which were acquired by following the procedure under the Land Acquisition Act.

It is also stated that as per Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the RFCTLARR Act, 2013'), if the person entitled to compensation shall not consent to receive it, or if there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to the title to receive the compensation or as to the apportionment of it

sentences.text: It is further stated that since there are disputes over the property with regard to the title, the respondents have deposited the amounts under Section 72(2) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not disputed the said fact.

5. In view of the said submissions, as the respondents have already deposited the compensation before the authority under Section 72(2) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of this writ petition relegating the petitioner to file an appropriate application before respondent No.4 for apportionment of the amounts awarded.

On filing of such application,
the respondents are directed to consider the same within a period of three (3) months from the date of filing of such application.
6. In view of the same, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
